Canva is THE BEST!! for small businesses
I’ve been using canva for the past few years now, but recently just opened up my own small business! I ordered 150 business cards and when they came in 8 out of 150 had some lines on them around the edges, I reached out to customer support just because I figured i’d let them know something was going on, not expecting anything because only 8 of the 150 were affected. They were very prompt to let me know that it wasn’t an issue on my side with sizing or the graphics, and something happened in the process of printing. They went ahead and immediately processed a new order, and included expedited shipping FOR FREE! I genuinely am not the person to reach out expecting free stuff or whatever because of a small inconvenience. I use canva for everything from business cards to photo editing, and now will never stop. Thanks to canva I’m not gonna need business cards for a long long time.

text: Limited Offline Functionality: Canva is primarily a cloud-based tool, meaning you need a stable internet connection to edit and save your designs. The desktop apps offer very limited offline capabilities. Pricing and Feature Paywalls: Many of the best templates, elements, stock photos, and advanced tools (like the one-click background remover and Magic Resize) are locked behind the Canva Pro subscription, which can be expensive for casual users or small teams. Exporting Restrictions: You cannot export designs as fully layered, editable source files (like PSD for Photoshop or AI for Illustrator). This can make it difficult if you ever need to transition a project to a professional graphic designer. Mobile App Clunkiness: While the mobile app is functional, complex editing tasks can feel cramped and frustrating on a smaller smartphone screen compared to the desktop version. Overused Templates: Because Canva is so incredibly popular, some of the most common free templates are highly recognizable, making it harder to create a totally unique brand identity without heavy customization. Rigid Text and Alignment Controls: For advanced designers, the typography tools, text wrapping options, and precision alignment grids can feel restrictive compared to dedicated publishing tools like Adobe InDesign.
